declarations.docstring: The degree-n k-module obtained from the linear Yoneda complex associated to a projective resolution and a coefficient module.
The degree-n additive commutative group attached to a left module and a projective resolution of an opposite-ring module.
A morphism between projective resolution complexes induces a morphism between their linear Yoneda complexes in the reversed direction.
The degree-n linear Yoneda objects for two projective resolutions are isomorphic.
A morphism of projective-resolution complexes induces, in the displayed direction, a map between degree-n linear Yoneda objects.
Under the displayed composition equality, the induced map on degree-n linear Yoneda objects is the hom of the specified isomorphism.
Two complex morphisms satisfying the displayed composition equalities induce equal maps on degree-n linear Yoneda objects.
The linear Yoneda complexes associated to two projective resolutions are homotopy equivalent.
The homology map induced by a compatible morphism of projective resolutions is the hom of the comparison isomorphism after applying an additive functor.
Two morphisms satisfying the displayed degree-zero composition equalities induce equal homology maps after applying an additive functor.
Applying an additive functor to two projective resolutions gives an isomorphism between their homology objects in every degree.
The hom of the additive-functor homology comparison isomorphism from a projective resolution to itself is the identity.
The composite of two additive-functor homology comparison isomorphisms agrees with the direct comparison isomorphism.
The degree-n groups attached to a left module and two projective resolutions of an opposite-ring module are isomorphic.
The hom of the module-pair group isomorphism from a projective resolution to itself is the identity.
The composite of two module-pair group isomorphisms equals the direct isomorphism.
A morphism of projective-resolution complexes induces a map on the associated degree-n module-pair groups.
Under the displayed composition equality, the induced map on degree-n module-pair groups is the hom of the specified isomorphism.
Two complex morphisms satisfying the displayed composition equalities induce equal maps on degree-n module-pair groups.
A homotopy equivalence of complexes in an opposite category yields a reversed homotopy equivalence between their unop complexes.
Any two projective resolutions of the same module have a nonempty type of homotopy equivalences between their complexes.
Between two projective resolutions of the same module, there exists a complex morphism satisfying the displayed composition equality.
